newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq, Bank Leumi in smartcard JV.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq, Bank Leumi in smartcard JV.

text.p: Israel's Bank Leumi and Bezeq Israel Telecom have agreed to set up a joint subsidiary which will issue payment smartcards, a newspaper said on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for Bank Leumi, the country's second-largest bank, refused to comment on the report. A bank source said the two companies were discussing such a venture but nothing had been finalised.
Bezeq officials could not be reached for comment.
The Globes financial daily said the smartcard would be based on the Visa credit card issued by Bank Leumi in Israel. It did not say when the subsidiary would be formed.

The smartcard is an electronic payment card introduced by banks and retailers around the world as an alternative to cash and checks. It also can be used for shopping and for person-to-person payments.

Israel's Discount Investment Corp and Paz Oil Co said last month they had acquired the franchise rights for another smartcard from London-based Mondex International Ltd, and would introduce it in Israel in the first quarter of 1998.
Mondex is majority owned by MasterCard International, with the remainder held by 27 other organisations in Europe, North America, Australia and Asia.
Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications provider, had an opportunity to join that venture but informed Paz and Discount it would not exercise the option, the newspaper said.
